testEnvironment:
Test environment: the snapshot is a git repository whose single commit holds
the reviewed tree — its tree hash was compared against the commit under review
when the snapshot was cut. A suite run here collects and runs what a checkout at
that commit does, so a failing or skipped test is a fact about the tree, not
about this copy of it. Its history is that one synthetic commit: 'git log',
'git diff' and every ancestry question answer about the snapshot and never about
the PR.
The Recipe's Test entrypoint and Check step do not run these merge-gating CI steps, and nothing in this review ran them: rebase-check job (pull_request-only branch-currency assertion, not meaningful in a worktree of origin/main); proc-macos job (node --test tests/proc.test.mjs on macOS) (subsumed by the full suite on this macOS host); smoke-omp job (needs pinned omp installed via bun, absent here); install-and-smoke job (needs pinned omp installed via bun and network, absent here).

survived.claim: The finisher gate's new Check 3 treats only ledger impl-N=PR#M tokens as the PR's own tickets. The phase-0 fold-in writes `PR#M · inherited (closes #N)` rows for a prior run's open ticket PR, and those rows carry no such token. Check 3 therefore refuses the finisher for that PR because its own ticket #N still carries in-progress. It then tells the controller to rewrite `Closes #N` as `Refs #N`, and following that advice makes the merge leave #N open and its claim stranded, which is the leak the ticket exists to stop.
survived.evidence: Appended to my copy's tests/ledger-dispatch.test.mjs: f.put("3606", `PR#3606 · inherited (closes #3545) · review=member:review-pr-3606 · reviewed=${GATE_HEAD}:0/0/0:${GATE_RUN}`); labelled(f.bin,3606,["patch"]); closes(f.bin,3606,[3545]); issueLabelled(f.bin,3545,["in-progress"]); f.ok("dispatch","3606","finisher-pr-3606"). Ran `node --test --test-name-pattern=PROBE tests/ledger-dispatch.test.mjs`, output: `✖ PROBE inherited ticket PR closing its own in-progress ticket … dispatch 3606 finisher-pr-3606: got exit 2  ledger: finisher-pr-3606: PR #3606 closes #3545, which another claim holds — rephrase it as "Refs #3545" — not dispatching finisher-pr-3606`. The row shape is the one phase0.mjs:548 writes (`PR#${pr.number} · inherited (${closes})`). Rotation after a dead run carries no impl token (phase-0.md:308-310). stranded.mjs leaves in-progress issues with an open PR to the fold-in (phase-0.md:587-588). next-ticket SKILL.md:193 says in-progress stays on the ticket until its PR merges. rulingOf (ledger.mjs:2015) builds `tickets` only from implementerClaims, and closingRefusals then calls claimedElsewhere(closed, tickets, …).
survived.suggested_fix: Also count as the PR's own the ticket N taken from its head branch when the head is a claim branch `implementer/<N>-impl-<N>[-x]`: read headRefName in the gate's prViewClosing call and add N to `own` before claimedElsewhere. Add a ledger-dispatch test for an inherited row whose PR closes its own in-progress ticket and is dispatched.

unverified.claim: The settle check calls issueLabels(n) once per occurrence. If closingIssuesReferences ever repeats a reference, the issue is read again and appears twice in the `in-progress: #7, #7` text. The finisher gate avoids the repeat read because it caches labels in a Map; settle does not.
unverified.evidence: Not executed. Reasoned from the diff: claimedElsewhere's `others.filter((n) => labelsOf(n).includes(inProgress))` has no dedupe, and settle passes `issueLabels` directly. I did not check whether ownClosingIssues already dedupes.

unverified.claim: The in-progress comparison is case-sensitive (`labelsOf(n).includes(inProgress)`), although the Label map treats role strings as the same when they differ only in case. A map spelling in-progress as 'In-Progress' lets an issue labelled 'in-progress' through, with no error and the check showing 'in-progress: none'.
unverified.evidence: Probe B in my copy: the map set `in-progress` to 'In-Progress', PR #6 closed [#5, #7], and issue #7 had label 'in-progress'. The settle returned outcome PR#6 and refused nothing. The existing `labels.includes(ready)` in labelRefusal compares the same way, so this matches the existing convention. Whether gh returns repo-canonical label case, which would remove the gap, I did not test.
unverified.suggested_fix: Compare `l.toLowerCase()` against `inProgress.toLowerCase()`, matching labelStringFaults's case-insensitive uniqueness rule, or state that exact case is required.

unverified.claim: In `settle --from-report`, the new `issueLabels` reads run even after an earlier check has already failed. A failed check does not stop the later reads, because check() collects failures. A PR that is not OPEN, or that does not close #N, therefore dies as exit 2 ('could not read issue #M's labels') where it would have been exit 3 with the failing check named. The real fault (wrong PR) is reported as a gh read failure. This is loud rather than swallowed, and the 'nothing written' message is accurate.
unverified.evidence: Probe A: state CLOSED, refs [#5, #7], no answer for issue 7. The settle exited 2 with 'could not read issue #7's labels … nothing written', and the CLOSED state was never reported. Probe A2: refs [#55, #7], PR does not close #5. Exit 2 naming #55's labels. The PR's own diff had to add `f.issue(55, {labels: []})` to the existing 'does not close ticket N' test to keep it at exit 3.
unverified.suggested_fix: Skip the claimedElsewhere read when the OPEN or closes-#N checks have already failed, e.g. guard on `pr.state === "OPEN" && numbers.includes(live.number)`. Or accept the exit-2 precedence and say so.

unverified.claim: I found no swallowed error, empty catch, or dereference moved inside an existing try in this diff. The only try/catch touched is `roleLabel`. Its body is the same `readLabelMap(...)[role]` call as before, generalised over the role, and it still re-throws anything that is not LabelMapUnreadable or FleetDirUnresolvable. Malformed gh answers (missing title, `labels` null, a non-array, or unnamed labels) all go through `die`, and the PR's own tests cover them. The Label map cannot hold `in-progress` as undefined: readLabelMap rejects a missing role via labelStringFaults. The `includes(inProgress)` check therefore cannot silently pass on an undefined string.
unverified.evidence: Read ledger.mjs roleLabel and namedLabels. Read label-map.mjs readLabelMap and labelStringFaults (stringFault returns 'missing' for undefined, which becomes LabelMapUnreadable). The test-run log shows 8869 of 8869 pass, including the new 'could not look' cases for a failed read, a bad shape, and an absent map.

unverified.claim: The stub comment (and the stub itself) still advertises `issue view <n> --json title`, but this diff moved the only caller (ledger.mjs issueRead) to `title,labels`, so no code path in the tree asks for `--json title` any more and the `title`-only branch is dead.

The comment reads as if the three field sets are all still exercised.
unverified.suggested_fix: Drop `--json title` from the comment and the `fields !== "title"` / `fields === "title"` branches, leaving `labels,state,title` and `title,labels`.

unverified.claim: The added sentence 'A ticket closed by another claim's PR strands that claim: neither release nor reap removes it' is ambiguous about 'it' and was not checked against release-ticket.sh or reap.sh behaviour.
unverified.evidence: Read release-ticket.sh header (lines 1-30): release only handles never-dispatched branches and branches whose PRs all read CLOSED, and reap.sh is named as handling merged tickets. I did not trace the stranded-claim path (closed issue plus in-progress label plus an unmerged claim branch) through either script, so the claim is unconfirmed.
unverified.suggested_fix: Name what is stranded (the claim's label, worktree and branch), or cite the script behaviour.

unverified.claim: claimedElsewhere(numbers, own, labelsOf) states in a comment, not in the code, that labelsOf(n) must return a string array. The closingRefusals caller passes `(m) => labels.get(m)`, which returns undefined for a number missing from the Map, and .includes would then throw a TypeError.
unverified.evidence: Read from the diff. closingRefusals sets labels for every n it pushes to `closed` and passes only `closed` to claimedElsewhere, so undefined is unreachable today. The other caller, issueLabels, goes through labelNames, which dies on anything but a named-label list. Nothing runs undefined through the invariant at runtime. The test run passed 8869/8869.
unverified.suggested_fix: Optional. Have closingRefusals collect the labels in a Map and pass `labels.get(m) ?? []`, or pass the Map's own getter and assert, so that a missing number fails loudly instead of throwing a TypeError. No change is required.

unverified.claim: In closingRefusals, the `closed` array is redundant state: prViewClosing's numbers come from ownClosingIssues, which deduplicates them through a Set in GitHub's order, so `closed` always holds exactly the keys of the new `labels` Map, in the same order.
unverified.evidence: closing-refs.mjs:25-36 builds `numbers = new Set()` and returns `[...numbers]`. In simplify/copy2 I removed `const closed = []` and `closed.push(n)` and added `const closed = [...labels.keys()];` after the loop. Then ran `node --test --test-reporter=tap tests/ledger-dispatch.test.mjs`: exit=0, # tests 144, # pass 144, # fail 0, which includes the PR's new claimed-elsewhere, Ticketless and duplicate-reference tests.
unverified.suggested_fix: Keep only the Map: `const labels = new Map(); for (const n of refs) { const issue = issueRead(n); if (issue.title.trim() === own) failures.push(...); else labels.set(n, issue.labels); } const closed = [...labels.keys()];` Then the claimedElsewhere loop and `return { refs: closed, failures }` stay as they are.

unverified.claim: Since this PR replaced ledger's issueTitle (`--json title`) with issueRead (`--json title,labels`), nothing sends `gh issue view <n> --json title` any more, so the GH_STUB's `fields !== "title"` acceptance and its `fields === "title" ? { title: issue.title } : …` branch are dead. The doc comment's `(or --json title, …)` is out of date too.
unverified.evidence: A grep for `--json title` / `"--json", "title"` over plugin/ and tests/ found only title,body,comments…, labels,state,title (dispositions-check.mjs:775) and title,labels (ledger.mjs:2121). In simplify/copy I took `&& fields !== "title"` out of the guard and replaced the ternary with the full `{ labels, state, title }` answer. Then ran `node --test --test-reporter=tap tests/dispositions-check.test.mjs`: exit=0, # tests 142, # pass 142, # fail 0, and `grep -c 'unexpected call'` on the log printed 0.
unverified.suggested_fix: Guard: `(fields !== "labels,state,title" && fields !== "title,labels")`. Answer: `process.stdout.write(JSON.stringify({ labels: issue.labels.map((name) => ({ name })), state: issue.state, title: issue.title }));`. Comment: `issue view <n> --json labels,state,title (or --json title,labels)`.
